slides.title: Work Experience Is Part of Your Course
slides.content: Work experience is not an optional extra. It helps you: Build your portfolio. Gain real workplace experience. Collect references. Strengthen applications. Test possible career paths.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Work Experience Is Part of Your Course'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Work Experience Is Part of Your Course.

slides.title: Why Work Experience Matters
slides.content: Work experience supports: Employability: Provides evidence employers can trust. Progression: Supports applications for university, apprenticeships and jobs. Professional Identity: Helps you discover which areas of the industry suit you best.

exercise.prompt: What is a key message of 'Why Work Experience Matters'?
options: It is only assessed in exams
It is optional and not required
Work experience supports: Employability: Provides evidence employers can trust
It applies only to certain students
exercise.explanation: Work experience supports: Employability: Provides evidence employers can trust

slides.title: Work Experience Can Take Different Forms
slides.content: Options may include: Block placements. Employer visits. Volunteering. Live project briefs. Industry partnerships. Not every option suits every course.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Work Experience Can Take Different Forms'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Work Experience Can Take Different Forms.

slides.title: If You Cannot Secure a Placement
slides.content: You can still take part through: Employer-set projects. Employer talks. Industry activities delivered in college. Skills Week is never wasted.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'If You Cannot Secure a Placement'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on If You Cannot Secure a Placement.

slides.title: Key Dates
slides.content: Important dates: **Skills Week:** 8 March 2027 **Placement Request Deadline:** 5 February 2027 Placement requests must be submitted early because employers require checks including: Health and safety checks. Insurance checks. Safeguarding checks.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Key Dates'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Key Dates.

slides.title: Using Navigate
slides.content: Before requesting a placement you need: Company name and address. Employer contact details. Dates and times. Tutor details. Placement role information. Navigate is accessed through: My Student Life. login.navigate.uk.com.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following is a key point about 'Using Navigate'?
exercise.explanation: This is a key point from the section on Using Navigate.

slides.title: Help Is Available
slides.content: If you need support: Contact Careers & Employability. Speak to your tutor. Ask for help early if a placement is not progressing. Support is available before and during placement.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Help Is Available'? Select all that apply.

exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Help Is Available.

slides.title: Expectations During Placement
slides.content: You should: Be punctual. Follow dress codes. Communicate professionally. Complete placement journals. Log hours accurately. Raise concerns quickly. Professional standards matter from day one.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Expectations During Placement'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Expectations During Placement.

slides.title: Placement Evidence Matters
slides.content: Employers value: References. Workplace experience. Demonstrated professionalism. A placement creates both experience and evidence.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Placement Evidence Matters'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Placement Evidence Matters.
